t.1.67.1: Clearly you are a king's daughter, O lovely one, judging by the way you speak. Become my wife, O fair-hipped one; tell me, what shall I do for you?
t.1.67.3: Today I shall bring you gold necklaces and the like, and hides as well; let the whole kingdom be yours today. Become my wife, O lovely one!
t.1.67.4: Come to me, timid one, by the Gāndharva form of marriage, O beautiful woman; for of all marriages, O lady with thighs like plantain stems, the Gāndharva is said to be the best.
t.1.67.5: My father has gone from this hermitage to gather fruit, O king. Wait for him a moment; he will give me to you.
t.1.67.2: Garlands of gold, garments, a pair of earrings and a pair of bracelets, gleaming and fashioned in many different cities, and lovely gems and jewels.
t.1.67.6: Duḥṣanta said: I desire you, O fair-hipped, faultless lady, to be devoted to me in return. Know that I stand here for your sake, for my mind has gone to you.
t.1.67.8: In brief, eight forms of marriage are traditionally recognized according to dharma: the Brāhma, the Daiva, likewise the Ārṣa, the Prājāpatya, and likewise the Āsura.
t.1.67.9: The Gāndharva, the Rākṣasa, and the Paiśāca, which is known as the eighth: Manu Svāyambhuva declared the laws of these in their proper order.
t.1.67.7: The self alone is the self's kinsman, and the self alone is the self's refuge; by your own self you may rightly make the gift of your self, in accordance with dharma.
t.1.67.11: For kings the Rākṣasa form is also declared proper, while the Āsura form is prescribed for Vaiśyas and Śūdras. Of the five forms, three are lawful and two are held to be unlawful here.
t.1.67.10: Understand that the first four are approved for a brāhmaṇa, and know, O blameless one, that six, in due order, are lawful for the warrior class.
t.1.67.13: Do not doubt that the Gāndharva and the Rākṣasa forms are lawful for the kṣatriya class; they may be practised separately or combined, of this there is no doubt.
t.1.67.12: The Paiśāca and the Āsura forms of marriage must never be performed under any circumstances. Marriage is to be made according to this rule; this is held to be the way of dharma.
t.1.67.14: So you, O fair-complexioned lady, desiring me as I desire you, ought to become my wife by the Gāndharva form of marriage.
t.1.67.15: Śakuntalā said: If this is indeed the path of dharma, and if I myself have authority over the giving away of myself, then hear my condition, O best of the Pauravas, O lord.
t.1.67.16: Promise me truly what I shall tell you in private: the son who may be born to me, let him be your successor after you.
t.1.67.18: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: "So be it," the king replied to her without hesitation, "and moreover, O sweetly smiling one, I will bring you to my own city, as you deserve, O fair-hipped one; this I tell you truly."
t.1.67.17: He shall be the crown prince, great king; tell me truly that this is so. If it is so, Duḥṣanta, then let my union with you take place.
t.1.67.19: Having spoken thus, the royal seer took her of faultless gait by the hand according to the rite, and he dwelt with her.
t.1.67.20: Having reassured her, he departed, and he said again and again: "I will send for your sake an army of four divisions; with it I will bring you to my own dwelling, O you of pure smiles."
t.1.67.22: "When the blessed one, endowed with ascetic power, hears of this, what will he do?" Thus brooding, he entered his own city.
t.1.67.21: Having thus given his promise to her, O Janamejaya, that king, the lord of the earth, departed, pondering in his mind about Kāśyapa.
t.1.67.24: And then Kaṇva, the blessed one of divine knowledge and great austerity, having understood her, seeing with his divine eye, spoke, well pleased.
t.1.67.23: When he had been gone but a short while, Kaṇva too returned to the hermitage; and Śakuntalā, out of shame, did not go to meet her father.
t.1.67.26: For the Gāndharva marriage is declared the best for a kṣatriya; it is traditionally held to be the union, without mantras and in private, of a desiring woman with a desiring man.
t.1.67.25: The union with a man that you, born of a royal line, entered into today without regard for me does not violate dharma.
t.1.67.27: Righteous and great-souled is Duḥṣanta, the best of men, whom you, Śakuntalā, approached as your husband, for he was devoted to you.
t.1.67.28: A great-souled son of yours, mighty in strength, will be born in the world, who will enjoy this entire earth bordered by the ocean.
t.1.67.31: That Duḥṣanta, the best of men, whom I have chosen as my husband, to him together with his ministers you should show your favor.
t.1.67.30: Then, having washed his feet, she spoke to him again once he had rested, after she had taken down his load and set the fruits in their place.
t.1.67.33: Then Śakuntalā, out of a desire for Duḥṣanta's welfare, chose as her boon righteousness for the Pauravas and likewise their never falling from the kingship.
t.1.67.29: And as that great-souled universal sovereign sets forth, his supreme wheel will forever roll on unobstructed.
t.1.67.32: For your sake, O fair-complexioned one, I am indeed pleased with him; and receive from me a boon, whatever you desire for his sake.
